title: Poland – Architectural design services – Konkurs architektoniczny na opracowanie koncepcji przebudowy Piekarni Rajcherta w Warszawie
description: Przedmiotem konkursu jest remont zabytkowej Piekarni Rajcherta z rozbudową i nadbudową na cele kultury w Dzielnicy Praga-Południe m.st. Warszawy w ramach zadania o nazwie: Modernizacja budynku dawnej piekarni przy ul. Grochowskiej 224 - prace przygotowawcze. Nowy obiekt ma stanowić nowoczesne, lokalne centrum kultury i aktywności mieszkańców o wyrazistej tożsamości wynikającej z historii miejsca. Obiekt ma łączyć codzienny i nieformalny pobyt użytkowników z zaplanowaną działalnością kulturalną, edukacyjną, społeczną, biblioteczną, gastronomiczną i wydarzeniową. Teren objęty konkursem położony jest w Warszawie w dzielnicy Praga-Południe, przy ul. Grochowskiej 224 i obejmuje działki ewidencyjne nr 127/13 i 132 oraz fragmenty działek ew. nr 127/18 i 127/26 z obrębu 3-04-06.

title: SWAG Cancer Alliance Lung Cancer Screening Programme
description: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust (BFT), as host organisation for the Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire (SWAG) Cancer Alliance, is seeking to appoint a provider to deliver a fully managed Lung Cancer Screening Programme across the Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire (SWAG) Cancer Alliance area. The procurement is being managed by Bristol and Weston NHS Purchasing Consortium (BWPC) on behalf of the Trust. The service will identify and engage eligible populations, deliver lung cancer screening services, provide low-dose CT (LDCT) scanning services, and ensure effective management of participant pathways in support of the early detection and diagnosis of lung cancer. The provider will be required to deliver a high-quality, accessible and equitable service that maximises uptake, reduces health inequalities, and complies with all relevant national standards and programme requirements. The contract term is 36 months, with the option to extend for up to two further periods of 12 months each, giving a maximum total contract duration of 60 months. Additional information is contained within the Invitation to Tender documentation available through SAP Ariba.

title: Request for Information: Flexoelectric Future
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Multi X Office (MXO) seeks information to inform possible future research on flexoelectric materials. The Department of War (DoW) requires sensing and transduction technologies that operate under size, weight, power, communications, and environmental constraints. The intended scope of this RFI is foundational materials, interfaces, metrology, design rules, and device elements that may encode or discriminate local mechanical state through strain-gradient-driven electromechanical response.

title: Switzerland – Electrical installation work – PWA-T3, T5, T6 (Selektiv) Ausschreibung Elektro, BKP 232 Niederspannungsinstallationen
description: Die Infrastruktur des Flughafens Zürich unterliegt einem schrittweisen Erneuerungsprozess. In den letzten 15 Jahren sind verschiedene Teile der zentralen Flughafeninfrastruktur umfassend saniert und erweitert worden: Das Dock B wurde komplett umgebaut, der Terminal 2 totalsaniert und erweitert, und zwischen den Terminal 1 und 2 wurde das neue Sicherheitskontrollgebäude mit zentralisiertem Zugang in das Airside Center erstellt. Derzeit werden die zentrale Gepäcksortieranlage nördlich des Terminal 1 erweitert und das flughafenweite Gepäcksortiersystem abgelöst und erneuert. In einem nächsten Schritt müssen die in die Jahre gekommenen Teile der zentralen Flughafen- Infrastruktur ersetzt werden: Das Dock A wurde zusammen mit dem Tower 1985 in Betrieb genommen und blieb in seiner Struktur bis heute weitgehend unverändert. Bezüglich Funktionalität, Nachhaltigkeit und Qualität kann das Dock A die heutigen Anforderungen nicht mehr erfüllen. Aufgrund einer umfassenden Analyse wurde entschieden, das bestehende Dock A durch einen Neubau nördlich des heutigen Gebäudes zu ersetzen. Der Ersatzneubau für das Dock A, der neue Tower und das umfassend sanierte Vorfeld zum Dock A mit allen weiteren Anpassungen, Erweiterungen und Umbauten der zentralen Flughafeninfrastruktur sind die sichtbar wichtigsten baulichen Massnahmen der nächsten 15 bis 20 Jahre. Bei der etappenweisen Realisierung muss gewährleistet werden, dass der Betrieb normal weitergeführt werden kann und mit den neu erstellten Gebäuden die künftigen funktionalen Anforderungen erfüllt werden können. Das Projekt PWA.T «Perimeterfreilegung Wurzel A» ist in drei Teilprojekte (T3, T5 und T6) unterteil und beinhaltet die Umsetzung von Anpassungen an bestehenden Medien und Anlagen. Diese befinden sich im und auch ausserhalb des Abbruchsperimeters der Wurzel Dock A. Die Arbeiten sind für den Bauzustand des Rückbaus und für die weiteren Phasen des Hauptprojekts Luftseite zu realisieren. Die Ausführung der vorliegenden Leistungen beginnt bereits 2027 und erfolgt etappiert; der Schwerpunkt liegt gemäss den indikativen Projektterminen (Kapitel IV, Ziffer 1.1) in den Jahren 2027 bis 2029. Nachgelagerte Etappen im Zusammenhang mit dem Hauptprojekt Luftseite können nach einer längeren Unterbrechung bis ca. 2033 folgen. Diese späten Termine dienen lediglich der Orientierung; sie entsprechen dem aktuellen Planungsstand und können sich im weiteren Projektverlauf ändern. Im Abbruchperimeter der Dockwurzel A sind essenzielle Teile der Gebäudetechnik für die Versorgung des Kontroll-Towers, Dockwurzel A, Dock A, Airside Center und der Passkontrollhalle verortet.

title: Denmark – Construction work – Udbud af ret til at virke som ladeoperatør af offentligt tilgængelige ladepunkter i Gentofte Kommune (Genudbud)
description: Dette udbud vedrører Gentofte Kommunens overladelse af retten til at virke som operatør af offent-ligt tilgængelige ladepunkter på kommunale vejarealer i Gentofte Kommune jf. Europa-parlamentets og Rådets forordning 203/1804 af 13. september 2023 om etablering af infrastruktur for alternative drivmidler og AFI-loven (LBK nr. 1043 af 17/09/2024 Bekendtgørelse af lov om infrastruktur for alternative drivmidler). Udbuddet gennemføres som et koncessionsudbud, jf. Direktiv 2014/23/EU om tildeling af koncessionskontrakter (Koncessionsdirektivet), da den samlede værdi af koncessionen forventes at udgøre DKK 220.000.000, hvilket er over tærskelværdien for EU-udbud (beregnet i overensstemmelse med den i Koncessionsdirektivets artikel 8, stk. 3 angivne metode ved anvendelse af Vejdirektoratets skabelon for beregning af koncessionsværdien). Udbudsmaterialet henviser derudover til LBK nr. 116 af 3. februar 2025, ”Udbudsloven” hvor relevant. Gentofte Kommune (Kommunen) har en eksisterende portefølje af koncessionskontrakter vedrørende retten til at virke som Ladeoperatør med forestående udløb, som derfor skal genudbydes. Derudover har Kommunen behov for at udbyde et antal nye lokationer som følge af øget behov og efterspørgsel på offentligt tilgængelige Ladepunkter i Gentofte Kommune. Udbuddet omfattet i alt 220 Ladepunkter. Af Bilag 3 Lokationsliste fremgår en oversigt over lokationer med angivelse af antal Ladepunkter til etablering på den konkrete lokation. Af Bilag 3 Lokationsliste fremgår det, om der er tale om et genudbud eller en ny-etablering af Ladepunkt. De enkelte lokationer er vurderet egnede ift. trafikale hensyn og placeret, hvor behovet og efterspørgslen vurderes størst. Det samlede antal Lokationer/Ladepunkter der udbydes er fordelt på ni delaftaler. Af Bilag 3 Lokationsliste fremgår, hvilke Lokationer der er omfattet af hvilke delaftaler. Ladeoperatøren har frit valg mht. hvilken type lader (normallader, hurtiglader eller lynlader) der op-stilles på lokationen, typen skal dog fremgå af tilbuddet og angives i Operatørens løsningsbeskrivelse for den enkelte delaftale. Kommunen udbyder alene retten til at virke som Ladeoperatør på de pågældende lokationer. Det er de bydendes opgave at skitsere løsning på de enkelte lokationer, herunder valg af type af lader (normal- hurtig- eller lynlader) samt antal Ladepunkter pr. Ladestander. Operatøren skal selv finansiere omkostningerne til etablering, drift og nedtagning af egne Ladepunkter. Hvor der i dag er etableret et Ladepunkt med udløb af koncessionskontrakt, skal Operatøren koordinere opstilling med den eksisterende operatørs nedtagning. Lokationerne udbydes som individuelle delaftaler. Der kan afgives tilbud på enkelte eller alle delaftaler, men samme tilbudsgiver kan ikke tildeles alle delaftaler, der henvises til afsnit 4.2 for nærmere beskrivelse af tildeling af delaftaler. Der indgås enslydende kontrakter for hver enkelt delaftale. Udbuddet gennemføres efter en proces, der svarer til offentligt udbud, hvor alle egnede leverandø-rer har adgang til at afgive tilbud.

Ireland – Railway construction works – TII499 Luas Finglas Main Infrastructure Design and Construction Works
description: Luas Finglas is a 4 km extension of the Luas Green Line, delivering a high-capacity light rail connection between Finglas and Dublin city centre to support sustainable transport and urban development. The scheme will serve communities including Charlestown, Finglas Village, Finglas West, St Helena’s, and the Tolka Valley, and will comprise four new stops at St Helena’s, Finglas Village, St Margaret’s Road, and Charlestown. It also includes a 350-space Park and Ride facility near St Margaret’s Road, as well as interchange opportunities with bus services and with mainline rail services at Broombridge. The Luas Finglas Main Infrastructure Design and Construction Works will be delivered under the NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract (ECC) Option C (Target Cost with Activity Schedule). The scope of this Contract (TII-499) includes, but is not limited to, the design and construction of the following principal elements: 1. Site clearance and demolitions. 2. Track (trackbed and rails). 3. Luas Stops at St Helena’s, Finglas Village, St Margaret’s Road and Charlestown. 4. Broombridge stabling site works. 5. Park and Ride facilities at St Margaret's Road. 6. Royal canal and rail overbridge at Broombridge. 7. Tolka Valley Park Bridge. 8. Fencing, retaining walls, boundary treatments and accommodation work. 9. Utility services realignment, diversion, replacement, and protection. 10. Road realignments and junction modifications. 11. Pedestrian and cycling facilities including cycle storage structures. 12. Road traffic signalling. 13. Landscape and urban realm upgrades. 14. Overhead Catenary System (OCS). 15. Power and Systems infrastructure. 16. Signalling, controls and other rail systems. 17. Working in live traffic environment on the busiest radial corridors in the greater Dublin area including property and business frontage reconfiguration. 18. Heritage / archaeology mitigation works. 19. Installation of stop furniture. 20. Installation of Validators and Ticket Vending Machines. 21. Other Ancillary works. The successful Contractor will also be responsible for: • Overall systems integration. • Interfacing and co-ordinating with other works packages to facilitate completion of works. • Interfacing and co-ordinating with stakeholders. • Testing and commissioning.

title: Landscaping and Snow Removal USCG TRACEN Cape May
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) AND INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. This notice is issued solely for market-research and planning purposes. It is not a solicitation, request for proposal, or commitment by the U.S. Coast Guard to award a contract or reimburse respondents for information or costs incurred in responding. The U.S. Coast Guard seeks industry feedback regarding a potential requirement for grounds maintenance, seasonal cleanup, landscaping support, and snow/ice-removal services at the U.S. Coast Guard Training Center (TRACEN) Cape May Family Housing Complex, 1 Munro Avenue, Cape May, New Jersey 08204. TRACEN Cape May maintains approximately 173 Coast Guard-owned family-housing units located in the 1400, 1500, 1600, 1700, and 1800 blocks, along with single-family homes and associated common areas. Common areas include lawns, sidewalks, walkways, parking areas, playgrounds, a basketball court, and bus stops. The anticipated requirement would include all personnel, supervision, equipment, tools, vehicles, materials, supplies, transportation, and incidental services necessary to perform routine grounds maintenance, seasonal cleanup, limited tree and shrub trimming, and snow/ice-removal services. Anticipated services include mowing, edging, trimming, weed removal or treatment, spring cleanup, fall cleanup, snow removal, and ice-control treatment for designated housing and common areas. Unless otherwise identified in the final requirement, services are not anticipated within fenced private backyards. The Government�s objective is to maintain housing-complex grounds, common areas, pedestrian routes, parking areas, and bus stops in a safe, neat, accessible, and usable condition. Routine grounds-maintenance services are anticipated principally during the growing season, generally April through November; snow and ice removal would be required in response to winter-weather events. title: BioWatch Program
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) SUMMARY: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), FEMA, Office of Resilience, Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) Support Directorate, requires support to staff identified local field offices and execute the daily BioWatch Program field operations in accordance with the attached Statement of Work (SOW). GENERAL INFORMATION: This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify sources that can provide support for the BioWatch program field operations, special events and surge operations, and technology upgrades and integration. In accordance with FAR 15.101(c), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. INTRODUCTION: DHS�s mission is to safeguard the American people, the homeland, and American values with honor and integrity. In support of this mission, the FEMA works to prevent CBRN attacks against the United States by providing timely, responsive support to operational partners. The CBRN Support Directorate advances this mission through the BioWatch program, the nation�s only civilian program that monitors for aerosol releases of select bioterrorism agents. Since its establishment in 2003, BioWatch has maintained a bioterrorism air monitoring system that operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week in large metropolitan areas, known as jurisdictions, and partnered with state and local public health communities to prepare for and respond to bioterrorist events. The BioWatch Program�s strategic objectives are to: Monitor for the highest-priority biological agents that could cause catastrophic outcomes. Protect the nation�s most at-risk locations. Maintain technical oversight of operations in close collaboration with state and local public health partners that execute the program. Conduct advanced development and use federal research and development (R&D) to procure and deploy improved detection capabilities at lower cost. Coordinate federal, state, and local public health preparedness activities to develop operational protocols for initiating response activities following the detection of an agent for which the system tests. Strengthen federal, state, and local stakeholder partnerships and improve operational efficiencies. To accomplish these objectives, each BioWatch jurisdiction maintains a static array of air samplers, the filters of which are collected daily by field operators. These filters are then delivered to a state or local operational laboratory where they are analyzed for select biological agents. Jurisdictions may also elect to surge operations by deploying additional units to monitor special events or increasing the collection cycle (e.g., twice a day collections). title: PAE Maritime PMS 500 Industry Day Announcement - DDG 1001 Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) DMP Technical Exchange
description: Industry Day Announcement in support of Naval Sea Systems Command (PAE Maritime). THIS NOTIFICATION IS BEING MADE TO PROVIDE PARTICIPANTS WITH THE MAXIMUM AMOUNT OF TIME FOR SCHEDULING AND MAKING TRAVEL ARRANGEMENTS. The program office for Guided Missile Destroyer (DDG) Zumwalt Class (PMS 500) intends to conduct an Industry Day in Washington, DC, on 9 Dec 2026. This Industry Day will be solely a technical exchange focused on the DDG 1001 Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) Depot Modernization Period (DMP). PMS 500 is conducting market research and technical dialogue to assess industry capability, technical execution strategies, and industrial capacity specifically in support of the upcoming DDG 1001 CPS DMP requirements. Program Background The DDG 1000 Zumwalt-class guided missile destroyers represent the Navy's premier multi-mission, stealth-oriented surface combatants, designed to deliver decisive long-range precision fires and operational deterrence. The overarching DDG 1000 Class Maintenance and Modernization strategy provides a synchronized, lifecycle framework to maintain class operational readiness, sustain advanced engineering systems, and field next-generation combat capabilities across all class hulls. A foundational element of this class-wide campaign is the incorporation of the Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) hypersonic weapon system capability on USS MICHAEL MONSOOR (DDG 1001) during her CPS Depot Modernization Period (DMP); May 2028 � Aug 2030. This modernization strategy encompasses: Hypersonic Payload Integration: Large-scale structural modifications, compartment reconfiguration, and integration of the Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) payload module and specialized launcher infrastructure to field prompt, long-range hypersonic strike capabilities. Combat System & Computing Infrastructure Upgrades: Comprehensive Total Ship Computing Environment Infrastructure (TSCEI) software/hardware modernization, open architecture enhancements, and tactical weapon control interfacing. Power & Thermal Management Expansion: Auxiliary plant enhancements, power conversion and distribution upgrades, and high-efficiency chilled water cooling modifications required to support advanced mission systems and weapon suites. Depot-Level Maintenance & Sustainment: Dry-docking evolutions, hull/mechanical/electrical (HM&E) overhaul, signature-managed hull preservation, and routine depot-level maintenance concurrent with major modernization packages. Within this broader class-wide maintenance and modernization framework, the upcoming DDG 1001 CPS DMP constitutes a critical execution milestone, demanding rigorous advance technical interchange between the Government and prospective industrial base performers to de-risk planning, interfaces, and industrial execution. Industry Day Purpose and Details PMS 500 will host this Industry Day solely as a technical exchange on the DDG 1001 CPS DMP. The primary intent is to engage in focused technical dialogue regarding the specific design, interface, production, schedule, and industrial execution challenges associated with this DMP, as well as to receive feedback from industry to refine technical requirements. PMS 500 will post a Requests For Information (RFI) containing targeted technical questions prior to the event, with the intent to conduct a technical exchange with Industry. PMS 500 is seeking attendance from companies that already possess a current PAE Maritime Master Ship Repair (MSR) Agreement and that demonstrate the technical capability and dry-dock/pier-side infrastructure necessary to execute the specialized industrial scope of the DDG 1001 CPS DMP. Companies that do not already possess a PAE Maritime MSR Agreement may participate if they intend to have such an agreement in place prior to the award and execution of the DMP. What / Where to Submit Companies that already possess a current PAE Maritime Master Ship Repair Agreement (MSRA): Email the primary and secondary points of contact listed in this announcement by December 04, 2026 at 12:00 PM Local Time, Washington D.C. with a subject line that states "DDG 1001 CPS DMP Technical Exchange Industry Day." The email should contain: Company name CAGE code Proposed attendee names, phone numbers, and email addresses (up to five (5) attendees only) All interested industry partners are welcome to register for this event. Please note that attendance is strictly limited to those Offerors who have submitted a formal response to the previously posted Sources Sought notice (N00024-26-R-4443). For those potential bidders who have not yet responded to the Sources Sought, but wish to attend, your Sources Sought response shall be submitted NLT 04 December 2026 in order to secure registration. Primary Points of Contact Lauren Welsh� lauren.g.welsh.civ@us.navy.mil Roger Sattler � roger.c.sattler4.civ@us.navy.mil Secondary Points of Contact Brian Romano � brian.c.romano.civ@us.navy.mil James Thomas � james.c.thomas118.civ@us.navy.mil Terms and Conditions Information provided shall be treated as Business Sensitive or Confidential to the responder, exempt from public release under the Freedom of Information Act. All information shall be provided free of charge to the Government. PAE Maritime may request further information regarding the capabilities of respondents to meet the requirements set forth in the announcement. This Industry Day announcement is released in accordance with FAR 15.201. This announcement is not a request for proposal. Information provided in response to this announcement will not be considered an offer by the responding contractor and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. No telephone inquiries will be accepted and requests for solicitation packages will not be granted, as a solicitation has not been prepared at this time. When to Submit: Responses are requested no later than 12:00 PM Local Time, Washington D.C. on 12/04/2026. Other: The Government will not pay for any effort expended or any material provided in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests, nor will the Government return any data provided. Future information, if any, will be posted at SAM.gov.

title: NETSAFA International Training Center Support
description: Amendment 2 posted 11/19/2026. Amendment 1 released on 11/4/2026 for Volume 1 Q and A responses. The Naval Education and Training Security Assistance Field Activity (NETSAFA), Pensacola, Florida, requires educational and training services, engineering and technical services, logistics, administration, management assistance, consulting and facilitation services, and transportation support services, training liaison, special mission personnel, and curriculum development. These services may be required in various locations in the U.S. or in foreign countries and may include support to foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs) under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP)/Security Assistance Training Program (SATP). The PSC code for this action is U099 Education/Training-Other associated with NAICS code 541330 under the Knowledge Based Services Taxonomy of services. NETSAFA supports international training in all warfare areas and at all levels of training for foreign countries. This is accomplished by staffing, operating, and managing international training support provided at NETSAFAs international training sites. The training sites are located in the NETASAFA International Training Center (NITC) located at Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida and NAS Whiting Field, Milton, Florida, and NITC Detachment Whiting Field, Milton, Florida. These sites are outfitted with computer training facilities, classrooms, and equipment needed to teach courses. They provide training and training support services in Navy activities such as government-owned contractor operating facilities. NETSAFAs international training sites are currently operational and have established curriculum. The training and other services required by this Performance Work Statement (PWS) are currently centered in four categories: General Training Programs, Aviation Training Programs, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs). Additionally, support will be required to meet emerging requirements in support of the SCETP/SATP. The instant requirement is for services associated with the international requirement of the United States and the foreign countries participating in the SCETP/SATP for a 12-month base period of performance beginning 01 March 2027 through 29 February 2028, with three (3) consecutive 12-month option periods pursuant to FAR 52.217-9, and a 6-month option period pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. The contractor will be required to periodically perform these services in various locations in the U.S. and may be required to perform these services in foreign countries. If support is needed in a foreign country, the contractor may be required to support foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, mobile training teams, and mobile education teams under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP) /Security Assistance Training Program (SATP).

title: Unison
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals for Unison, a program to develop and evaluate collaborative-autonomy approaches that jointly adapt team decision-making and communications during mission execution. Unison will investigate approaches that enable autonomous teams to modify tactics, behaviors, coordination relationships, and information exchange as mission complexity and operational variability increase and communications become constrained and/or degraded (see Section 7, Glossary, for program-specific definitions of terms in italics). The core hypothesis of Unison is that a unified execution-time reasoning approach to action planning and communications planning can improve the effectiveness, scalability, and resilience of collaborative autonomy in dynamic, uncertain, and resource-constrained environments. Unison seeks to preserve mission performance while reducing communication dependence and bounding the reasoning burden imposed on individual agents. Unison frames collaborative autonomy as a multi-agent decision problem in which agents use local observations, mission context, relevance, and mission objectives to select a policy that jointly defines physical actions and communications actions. At each decision point, the team must determine what actions to take, which coordination relationships must be maintained, and what information must be exchanged to preserve the coordination required for mission success. Unison will investigate approaches across teams of tens to hundreds of agents operating in representative collaborative, multi-domain mission scenarios.

title: Unison
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals for Unison, a program to develop and evaluate collaborative-autonomy approaches that jointly adapt team decision-making and communications during mission execution. Unison will investigate approaches that enable autonomous teams to modify tactics, behaviors, coordination relationships, and information exchange as mission complexity and operational variability increase and communications become constrained and/or degraded (see Section 7, Glossary, for program-specific definitions of terms in italics). The core hypothesis of Unison is that a unified execution-time reasoning approach to action planning and communications planning can improve the effectiveness, scalability, and resilience of collaborative autonomy in dynamic, uncertain, and resource-constrained environments. Unison seeks to preserve mission performance while reducing communication dependence and bounding the reasoning burden imposed on individual agents. Unison frames collaborative autonomy as a multi-agent decision problem in which agents use local observations, mission context, relevance, and mission objectives to select a policy that jointly defines physical actions and communications actions. At each decision point, the team must determine what actions to take, which coordination relationships must be maintained, and what information must be exchanged to preserve the coordination required for mission success. Unison will investigate approaches across teams of tens to hundreds of agents operating in representative collaborative, multi-domain mission scenarios.

description: SOURCES SOUGHT / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) MARKET RESEARCH FOR WOLF CREEK POWERHOUSE BRIDGE CRANE REHABILITATION DISCLAIMER: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE BEING RELEASED PURSUANT TO THE REVOLUTIONARY FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION OVERHAUL (RFO) PART 10: MARKET RESEARCH. PROJECT SCOPE OF WORK The contemplated requirement is for a firm-fixed-price standalone contract for the complete rehabilitation of the existing powerhouse bridge crane and incidental related work at the Wolf Creek Powerhouse in Jamestown, Kentucky. Crane Description: The existing powerhouse bridge crane is a 250-ton, top-running bridge type crane consisting of two bridge girders and two independent trolleys. Each existing trolley features: One (1) Main Hoist rated at 125 tons One (1) Auxiliary Hoist rated at 25 tons Major Work Items: The Contractor will be responsible for furnishing all labor, materials, supervision, engineering, tooling, and equipment required to complete the rehabilitation, which includes, but is not limited to, the following major items: Safety & Access: Modify personnel access and implement safety improvements to the bridge crane walkways, ladders, and maintenance platforms. Couplings & Seals: Replace hoist motor output shaft brake wheel coupling seals. Braking Systems: Replace hoist brake pads and perform comprehensive service to restore proper brake gap and operational torque. Gearboxes & Lubrication: Clean speed reducers (main hoist, auxiliary hoist, bridge drive, and trolley drive) and replace all lubricating oil; inspect and repair grease lubrication lines; replace main hoist open gear oil. Wheel & Axle Assemblies: Modify bridge and trolley wheel assemblies to replace original wheel bushings with new anti-friction roller bearings. (Note: The Contractor may have the option to replace entire wheel and axle assemblies or modify and reuse existing wheels and axles). Below-the-Hook Devices: Provide new, and perform non-destructive inspection, proof-load testing, and painting of below-the-hook lifting devices. Drives & Automation: Upgrade all variable frequency drives (VFDs) to Magnetek Series 5 VFDs (or approved system equal). Electrification & Grounding: Furnish and install a new fourth conductor bar dedicated as a continuous ground conductor; modify existing collectors to connect to the fourth conductor bar. Operator Cab & Controls: Provide and install a new ergonomic operator�s chair, wireless radio remote controllers, absolute hoist encoders, and high-efficiency LED bridge crane lights. Safety Instrumentation & Limits: Install load cell weighing devices and displays for both main and auxiliary hoists, along with new heavy-duty limit switches for bridge and trolley travel. Auxiliary Hoists: Furnish and install a new auxiliary tool hoist and a dedicated personnel rescue hoist. Testing & Commissioning: Perform full operational testing of all mechanical and electrical features of the crane, followed by 100% rated and 125% rated load tests in accordance with CMAA and OSHA requirements. Documentation: Develop and deliver a comprehensive new Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Manual integrating all legacy data from the existing manual with new equipment data to serve as a complete standalone guide. Blocks, Sheaves & Lifting Beams: Provide new main and auxiliary lower load block assemblies. Provide new main and auxiliary upper sheaves and pins. Provide new main hoist lifting beam, rotor lifting device, and turbine shaft lifting device. 15.Crane Runway Rails: Survey and modify existing runway crane rails to correct rail span, elevation, and straightness along the entire runway length. 3. title: BioWatch Program
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) SUMMARY: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), FEMA, Office of Resilience, Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) Support Directorate, requires support to staff identified local field offices and execute the daily BioWatch Program field operations in accordance with the attached Statement of Work (SOW). GENERAL INFORMATION: This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify sources that can provide support for the BioWatch program field operations, special events and surge operations, and technology upgrades and integration. In accordance with FAR 15.101(c), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. INTRODUCTION: DHS�s mission is to safeguard the American people, the homeland, and American values with honor and integrity. In support of this mission, the FEMA works to prevent CBRN attacks against the United States by providing timely, responsive support to operational partners. The CBRN Support Directorate advances this mission through the BioWatch program, the nation�s only civilian program that monitors for aerosol releases of select bioterrorism agents. Since its establishment in 2003, BioWatch has maintained a bioterrorism air monitoring system that operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week in large metropolitan areas, known as jurisdictions, and partnered with state and local public health communities to prepare for and respond to bioterrorist events. The BioWatch Program�s strategic objectives are to: Monitor for the highest-priority biological agents that could cause catastrophic outcomes. Protect the nation�s most at-risk locations. Maintain technical oversight of operations in close collaboration with state and local public health partners that execute the program. Conduct advanced development and use federal research and development (R&D) to procure and deploy improved detection capabilities at lower cost. Coordinate federal, state, and local public health preparedness activities to develop operational protocols for initiating response activities following the detection of an agent for which the system tests. Strengthen federal, state, and local stakeholder partnerships and improve operational efficiencies. To accomplish these objectives, each BioWatch jurisdiction maintains a static array of air samplers, the filters of which are collected daily by field operators. These filters are then delivered to a state or local operational laboratory where they are analyzed for select biological agents. Jurisdictions may also elect to surge operations by deploying additional units to monitor special events or increasing the collection cycle (e.g., twice a day collections). In addition, each jurisdiction has an advisory committee that coordinates with the BioWatch program on operations and biological event preparedness activities. At the federal level, the BioWatch program includes field, surge, laboratory, and biodefense preparedness operational components. Figure 1 depicts daily sample operations. Figure 1. BioWatch Sample Operational Process PURPOSE OF RFI Currently field operators and field-related tasks are not staffed by contract. The purpose of this RFI is to evaluate and determine the field staffing and support options for the BioWatch program to meet field operations requirements. The performer must enable the BioWatch program to maintain current field operations and continue to provide high quality, reliable, and timely delivery of field samples to the laboratories. In addition, due to its evolving operational needs, the performer must provide the necessary flexibility and adaptability to ensure BioWatch can address changes in sample collections for both planned events and unforeseen incidents, as well as assist with potential technology assessments, field evaluations, integration, and implementation. DESIRED CAPABILITIES FOR BIOWATCH FIELD STAFFING AND SUPPORT CAPABILITY Competent, proficient, and reliable field staffing is essential to ensure the BioWatch program continues to meet established requirements. In addition, the evolving threats and vulnerabilities that are identified at the state and local level require operational flexibility and adaptability that must be able to be supported with field staff capable of performing field operations and chain of custody in accordance with mission needs. A successful candidate staffing performer will provide field personnel to conduct BioWatch daily operations in select metropolitan cities within the United States. Composition and hierarchy of field staff at each location will be made at the discretion of the performer, with recommendations and concurrence from the BioWatch program. The staffing performer shall: Provide a Program Manager for the contract who will serve as the primary point of contact for the BioWatch Program and DHS Contracting Officer. Provide a primary point of contact, or lead, for each jurisdiction who will provide direct oversight of field staff and be responsible for administrative activities such as: Scheduling field staff and scoping collection routes. Maintaining appropriate documentation (e.g., training documentation, required inventories, etc.) Coordinating delivery times with local BioWatch laboratory. Communicating and coordinating with the BioWatch Field Operations team. Participating in relevant program meetings. Upon request, participating in local advisory committee meetings. Responding to requests for information from the BioWatch program. Supporting program audits and other assessments. Provide local office space to include space for equipment and consumable supplies storage. Implement staff recruitment and retention practices to maintain staffing levels over the life of the contract to: Support routine daily operations 7 days a week, 365 days a year and may require working beyond a standard 8-hour day and/or alternate shifts. Support planned and limited notice special events and surge operations (i.e., equipment deployment/demobilization, increased operations tempo, increased collection cycle, expanded array, etc.). Support changes to the static array (i.e., additions/reductions in number of collection sites) or collection routes. Ensure the staffing level in a given jurisdiction does not fall below 75% for longer than 1 month and that overall staffing levels do not fall below 90% per year. Accommodate appropriate and reasonable time off for personnel (i.e., paid time off, etc.) without compromising operations including special events and surge operations. Provide continuity of operations, which may include: Changes in operational tempo caused by limited notice special events. Travel of field staff from one jurisdiction to another for either surge support or to ensure continued steady-state operations. Perform all required operational tasks in accordance with the Field Operations Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and other program guidance, processes, and protocols, including: Logistics support. Equipment and supplies ordering and inventory maintenance and reporting. Ensure all field staff, including new hires, are appropriately trained in all relevant BioWatch operations procedures, processes, and protocols. Training materials are provided by the BioWatch program but the performer may be required to develop, maintain, and provide additional training to meet and support program objectives. Ensure field

description: The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) intends to negotiate and award a sole source Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) to Argo Turboserve Corporation (ATC) as the only Authorized Distributor representing Curtiss Wright for OEM hardware components and support services for High Pressure (HP) and Low Pressure (LP) Propulsion Turbine Rotors and Propulsion Turbine and Ship Service Turbine Generator Overhaul Kits. The Government intends to make an award prior to the 4th quarter of fiscal year 2027. The contractor shall provide Steam Propulsion Plant HP and LP Propulsion Turbines and associated components in overhaul kits as part of the Steam Critical Spares Program. Curtiss-Wright Steam and Air Solutions owns and utilizes proprietary information and technical data to manufacture the required hardware, which have has been shock and vibration qualified. Curtiss-Wright Steam and Air Solutions was selected as the OEM for the High Pressure (HP) and Low Pressure (LP) Propulsion Turbines during the shipbuilding phase of the LHD-1 and LCC-19 Class of vessels. title: NETSAFA International Training Center Support
description: Amendment 2 Released on 11/19/2026 Amendment 1 released on 11/4/2026 for Volume 1 Q&A responses. The Naval Education and Training Security Assistance Field Activity (NETSAFA), Pensacola, Florida, requires educational and training services, engineering and technical services, logistics, administration, management assistance, consulting and facilitation services, and transportation support services, training liaison, special mission personnel, and curriculum development. These services may be required in various locations in the U.S. or in foreign countries and may include support to foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs) under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP)/Security Assistance Training Program (SATP). The PSC code for this action is U099 Education/Training-Other associated with NAICS code 541330 under the Knowledge Based Services Taxonomy of services. NETSAFA supports international training in all warfare areas and at all levels of training for foreign countries. This is accomplished by staffing, operating, and managing international training support provided at NETSAFAs international training sites. The training sites are located in the NETASAFA International Training Center (NITC) located at Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida and NAS Whiting Field, Milton, Florida, and NITC Detachment Whiting Field, Milton, Florida. These sites are outfitted with computer training facilities, classrooms, and equipment needed to teach courses. They provide training and training support services in Navy activities such as government-owned contractor operating facilities. NETSAFAs international training sites are currently operational and have established curriculum. The training and other services required by this Performance Work Statement (PWS) are currently centered in four categories: General Training Programs, Aviation Training Programs, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs). Additionally, support will be required to meet emerging requirements in support of the SCETP/SATP. The instant requirement is for services associated with the international requirement of the United States and the foreign countries participating in the SCETP/SATP for a 12-month base period of performance beginning 01 March 2027 through 29 February 2028, with three (3) consecutive 12-month option periods pursuant to FAR 52.217-9, and a 6-month option period pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. The contractor will be required to periodically perform these services in various locations in the U.S. and may be required to perform these services in foreign countries. If support is needed in a foreign country, the contractor may be required to support foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, mobile training teams, and mobile education teams under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP) /Security Assistance Training Program (SATP).

title: Intent to Sole Source - Acquisition of ELITE Service Contract for Two (2) Luminex instruments
description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a request for proposal. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC) intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with the following vendor: Luminex Corporation. Acquisition Description: The service agreement is for two FM3D instruments that are used by the HLA Lab for daily testing of transplant patients and donors. The instruments are utilized to provide low resolution HLA typing results for multiple protocols at the NIH. Several of these protocols are for transplants. The ELITE Service Plan provides the following coverage: � Unlimited visits for emergency repair (includes travel, parts and labor) � Two preventative maintenance visits per year � Priority scheduling for service requests � Certain software updates and modifications � Telephonic and online support 24 x 7 Response Time: On-site one business day response time for repair service. On-site arrival by end of next business day when dispatch determination is made by 6pm Central Standard Time (CST). This level of service and response is required by the HLA Lab to ensure the instruments are functioning properly. Any down time to an instrument can result in delayed testing turn-around time. Many of the patients who utilize the HLA Lab services are transplant patients and donors. Prompt testing is essential for the transplant protocols. The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 253(c) (1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 only one responsible source and no other supply of service will satisfy agency requirements. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. Training Consultation for Program Revision; Development of Interactive eLearning Content. USPTO�s Patent Training Academy is the training program responsible for preparing new hires to be patent examiners. It is designed to give new examiners the skills, knowledge, and confidence they need to begin their careers. In FY 2026, the USPTO hired 963 new examiners. Currently, the training program is delivered over 10-weeks and is comprised of a 125-course curriculum. The program follows a university-style model that uses a mix of large-lectures and small group lab sessions to give examiners opportunity to apply what they have learned. Through a combination of the use of a practice training application, active learning exercises, lecture and dedicated examination time, the goal of the program is to provide patent examiner new-hires the needed competencies to successfully examine in a Technology Center (TC) with guidance from experienced examiners. OBJECTIVE The USPTO seeks a training partner/partners, that can bring innovative approaches, fresh ideas, and creative solutions to help modernize and strengthen the Patent Training Academy�s content and training delivery. The objective of this RFI is to seek capable contractors who could provide the USPTO with Training Consultation for Program Revision, and Development of Interactive eLearning Content. REQUIREMENTS Training Consultation for Program Revision: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in instructional design consultation services to provide innovative, modern, and forward-looking solutions that introduce new ideas, enhance learner engagement, and create a more effective, scalable, and future-ready training experience for patent examiners, to include: Expertise in instructional design and adult learning theories and principles. Experience providing innovative solutions to enhance engagement and learning in large training programs with extensive curriculums, specifically more than 40 courses in a single curriculum. Experience with providing reimagined experiential learning solutions including Super Intelligence (SI) to enhance learning and taking complex, detailed curriculum and transforming the curriculum to provide faster acquisition of job skills and application of content. Experience in incorporating SI solutions into training delivery models. All SI solutions must be approved by USPTO. Ability to work with subject matter experts to elevate learning objectives and ensure content alignment with learning objectives for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and upgrade course activities for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and modernize course teaching methodology for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to recommend updated assessments of learning objectives and outcomes. Experience in providing consultation services for legal content. Ability to develop training content and related deliverables in fresh, exciting, and engaging ways with a strong emphasis on immersive and technology-enabled experiential learning solutions with a focus on gamification and simulation-based learning . Experience in recommending appropriate scheduling for redesigned training programs. Ability to recommend ideal learning environment and delivery method, to include in-person learning classroom set-up, classroom technology requirements, hybrid learning delivery, and eLearning content at both headquarters and alternate locations. Ability to recommend fresh and innovative experiential learning solutions, and to provide a range of options in response to unique learning concerns. Development of Interactive eLearning Content: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in the development and implementation of cutting-edge, interactive eLearning content that uses innovative instructional design, interactive learning strategies, artificial intelligence-enabled solutions, gamification, adaptive learning, immersive technologies, contemporary and immersive visual design, dynamic visual elements, and cutting-edge ideas for improving learner engagement and knowledge retention, to include: Expertise in the design of eLearning content, using standard eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline 360, Adobe Captivate, and similar platforms, including SI-enabled development features where appropriate. All training content must be developed in a shareable and editable file format, firms must not recommend proprietary software or learning management system-solutions. title: Replacement TAO Wind Monitors for the National Data Buoy Center at Stennis Space Center, MS
description: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration�s (NOAA) Acquisition and Grants Office, Eastern Acquisition Division-Kansas City intends to negotiate and award a purchase order, on a sole source basis, under authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, with RM Young Company for Replacement TAO Wind Monitors (P/N 05103-1) to be delivered to National Data Buoy Center at Stennis Space Center, MS. The sole source determination is based on NOAA�s only one source is capable rationale. The RM Young propeller wind monitors technology uses magnetic induction for measuring wind speed which requires no energy input. Essentially you get the wind speed for free with respect to power requirements. Further, the directional portion of the sensor only requires 0.6 mW of power. That is 100 times less power requirement than an ultrasonic anemometer. This low power wind measurement is imperative in a battery-operated remote buoy station. The propeller anemometer also provides for the measurement of wind gusts over 100 m/s where no ultrasonic anemometer technology can currently measure in that range. The NDBC helped develop the R.M. Young propeller anemometer which is now considered the industry standard. No other propeller anemometer available has the reliability of the R.M. Young propeller anemometer. Hence, the R.M. Young model 05103-1 anemometer was selected as the anemometer for the TAO refresh system in 2010 and the TAP Recapitalization effort in 2023. The NDBC now has a complete TAO network populated with these 015103-1 wind monitors and this procurement replaces those units lost at sea, damaged beyond repair, or have reached their end of life during fiscal years 2025 and 2026. The RM Young 05103-1 is provided with the cable and connector required to match current TAO cabling. The 05103-1 also provides a pulse output for wind speed as a result of the magnetic induction technique for the measurement. The selection of another manufacturer�s wind sensors could result in $100K of engineering efforts to rework the hardware and firmware of the TAO system and the NDBC wind tunnel testing equipment to accept different connections and output formats. Further, due to TAOs climate study the new sensor would need to be tested side-by-side the RM Young 05103-1 for a year to develop the transition equation to ensure there are no step or abrupt changes in the general wind speed and direction trends. This year long side-by-side testing could cost more than $100k as it would require a co-located buoy at several locations. This pre-solicitation notice is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation package is available. However, firms that believe they can fully meet the government�s requirements may submit substantiating documentation or a request for additional information in writing to Abigail Green at Abigail.green@noaa.gov within 15 days after publication of this pre-solicitation notice. Such requests and documentation will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the government not to conduct a competitive procurement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this pre-solicitation notice.

title: Enterprise Workspace Management Support
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS PUBLISHED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. This notice is issued by the Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA HQ), on behalf of NAVSEA Facilities (Enterprise Workspace Management). NAVSEA is comprised of Headquarters (HQ) activities located at the Washington Navy Yard (WNY) and technical/industrial field organizations across more than 40 geographically dispersed activities spanning over 34 million gross square feet of facilities and supporting approximately 80,200 personnel. NAVSEA Facilities seeks to identify potential sources interested in and capable of fulfilling the requirements for enterprise workspace management support services to implement, sustain, expand, configure, and improve the ARCHIBUS Workplace Management System (IWMS) / Computer-Aided Facility Management (CAFM) platform. The current baseline utilizes ARCHIBUS version 25.2 (and approved upgrades) hosted across staging, testing, training, and production environments by the Enterprise Digital Capabilities (EDC) team at NSWC Dahlgren, VA. The requirement encompasses NAVSEA HQ, Program Executive Offices (PEOs), and participating field activities, including Naval Warfare Centers (NSWC/NUWC), Naval Shipyards (Norfolk, Pearl Harbor, Portsmouth, Puget Sound), Regional Maintenance Centers (CNRMC, MARMC, SERMC, SWRMC), Supervisors of Shipbuilding (SUPSHIP Bath, Groton, Gulf Coast, Newport News), and related naval commands. (Incumbent Contract Reference: Currently satisfied under SeaPort Task Order N00178-14-D-8048-EH01 by BlueWater Federal Solutions, Inc. Estimated LOE is approximately 240,910 Direct Labor Hours over a 5-year period of performance: one 12-month base year plus four 12-month option years). This requirement may include the following efforts: Provide full lifecycle day-to-day ARCHIBUS system administration, user account lifecycles, security groups, Virtual Private Archives (VPAs), user roles, dashboard design, workflows, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Execute field-activity site rollout plans using Agile processes to incorporate stakeholder requirements, assess site constraints, deploy licensed modules, and deliver formal Site Rollout Completion Packages. Maintain capacity to execute rollouts at up to five (5) field activities simultaneously when surge capacity is required. Establish and validate data integrity, GeoHierarchies, and organizational structures linking personnel, room/cubicle space, telecommunications, and IT hardware assets. Perform authorized interior and exterior LiDAR/3D laser scanning, building feature surveys, and facility asset verification in accordance with Government CAD/BIM standards (e.g., USACE CAD Standards). Execute CAD polylining, drawing conversion, layer standardizations, and Building Information Modeling (BIM) publishing and integration into ARCHIBUS. Provide robust prime-contractor quality control, oversight, and deliverable validation for any subcontractor-performed survey, scanning, or CAD/BIM efforts prior to Government submission. Develop, test, and sustain automated daily data feeds between source systems, legacy databases, and the ARCHIBUS production database hosted in the Enterprise Digital Capabilities (EDC) environment. Prepare, package, and document Configuration Change Requests (CCRs), staging test scripts, release notes, user-impact assessments, and rollback plans, supporting testing and deployment from Navy Marine Corps Intranet (NMCI) client environments. Facilitate stakeholder alignment sessions, business process mapping, and change-readiness activities across enterprise leadership and field activity commands. Develop role-based training curriculums, interactive guides, quick-reference aids, and SOPs; conduct hands-on training within the dedicated ARCHIBUS training environment prior to local go-live events. Accomplish full operational transition within a six (6) week phase-in period post-award, maintaining an Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), Quality Control Plan (QCP), and structured risk/issue registers. Ensure all personnel are U.S. citizens possessing a favorably adjudicated Federal Background Investigation at the Tier 3 (T3) level for Common Access Card (CAC) credentials and Navy IT network access. Maintain an adequate cost accounting system approved by DCAA/DCMA (FAR 16.301-3 / SF 1408) to support a CPFF task order.

title: St. Marys River Sea Lamprey Trap (SLT)
description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLCITATION NOTICE. THIS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR INVITATION FOR BID. The US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District is seeking contractors with the capability to provide construction services for the St. Marys River Sea Lamprey Trap (SLT) project. This project consists of construction of a sea lamprey trap structure downstream of Gate 16 of the St. Marys River Compensating Works in Chippewa County, MI. The project will involve installing a steel grating platform, trap vault, and lift system. The steel-grating platform will be 11-feet-long and 8-feet-wide and be supported by steel members fixed to a concrete wingwall. The trap vault will be composed of steel plates and fixed to the required platform and the existing concrete sill. The lift system will include one free-standing jib crane with a minimum rating of 1 ton. Demobilize when complete. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS are available for this Notice. The Government intends to solicit this opportunity as an Invitation for Bid (IFB). The IFB is intended to be issued Unrestricted as Full and Open Competition, and the Government intends to award to the lowest priced bid that is determined to be responsible and responsive. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this work is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction, which has a small business size standard of $45.0 million in average annual receipts. General Information: The Government intends to issue a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Construction Contract. Anticipated Solicitation Posting Date: December 2026 Anticipated Bid Due Date: January 2027 The estimated date for completion of work is July 2028 The estimated magnitude of construction is between $500,000 and $1,000,000. Product Service Code is Y1KA � Construction of Dams. Contractors can access SAM free of charge at www.sam.gov. The solicitation posted on SAM.gov will include a link to all solicitation documents which will be stored in the Solicitation Module of the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) system. Contractors may register for PIEE free of charge at https://piee.eb.mil/. In order for interested contractors to conduct business with the Federal Government, contractors must be registered in PIEE prior to the bid due date and in SAM.gov prior to any award. Hard copy documents will NOT be supplied by the Government to any interested parties as a result of this Pre-Solicitation Notice or the upcoming solicitation. Electronic bid submissions will be required through the PIEE Solicitation Module suite at https://piee.eb.mil/. Please note the Government will not be maintaining a bidders list during the solicitation period. title: HYDROSPHERE, BIOSPHERE, & GEOPHYSICS (HBG) SUPPORT SERVICES II - FINAL REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (FRFP)
description: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), hereby invites interested parties to review the Final Request for Proposal (FRFP) for the Hydrosphere, Biosphere, and Geophysics (HBG) Support Services II requirement supporting the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. The principal purpose of this requirement is to provide science research that conceives, develops, and applies space, field-deployed (i.e. airborne and in situ) and laboratory based technologies and observations to address issues of importance to society. These include but are not limited to water resources, land and ocean ecosystems, global and regional sea level change, changes in the Earth�s cryosphere, gravity field, magnetic field, solid Earth, and the terrestrial reference frame. The Statement of Work, Attachment A, describes the scope of the requirement. This contract is for support of a full range of science and research activities across the breadth of the various Laboratories that make up the HBG sub-division: the Cryospheric Sciences, Ocean Ecology, Hydrological Sciences, Biospheric Sciences, and Geodesy and Geophysics Laboratories. This contract is also for support of science, research and computing activities within the Terrestrial Information Systems Laboratory (TISL), also in the ESD. For the purposes of this document and contract the term HBG will be used to encompass all the Laboratories of the HBG sub-division and the TISL. NASA will conduct this acquisition as a small business set-aside. This competitive acquisition was originally contemplated as a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with the ability to issue CPFF task orders. Following further acquisition planning and assessment of the Government's requirements, the contract structure has been modified. The HBG II Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP) posted on April 8, 2025 was issued as an IDIQ CPFF solicitation. As amended, this competitive acquisition will now result in a HYBRID Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with the ability to issue Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) AND Firm- Fixed Price (FFP) task orders. The contract will have an effective ordering period of five years from the contract effective date. Interested offerors are encouraged to review the solicitation and all associated attachments for complete details regarding the requirements and proposal submission instructions. Please see the attached cover letter for additional information.

title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLICIT FROM A SINGLE SOURCE - Environmental Modeling Technical Support and EEMS Workshop Jacksonville Harbor Deepening Project
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLICIT FROM A SINGLE SOURCE Environmental Modeling Technical Support and EEMS Workshop Jacksonville Harbor Deepening Project Proposed Source: DSI, LLC | UEI: MBMESK928KP3 The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Jacksonville District, intends to solicit and award a firm-fixed-price contract to DSI, LLC, on a single-source basis pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) RFO 6.302-1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. This notice is issued to inform industry of the Government�s intent and to invite capability statements from firms that believe they can meet the requirement. This is not a request for quotations or proposals; no solicitation is available at this time. The requirement supports the Jacksonville Harbor Deepening Project�s environmental modeling activities, including assessment of salinity conditions in the Lower St. Johns River. The anticipated period of performance is 12 months. The required services include: � Preparation of customized workshop materials using the Government�s existing Jacksonville Harbor modeling files and relevant assessment scenarios; � One five-day, instructor-led, hands-on workshop for Government personnel covering the current EFDC+ Explorer Modeling System (EEMS), including EFDC+, EFDC+ Explorer, and Grid+, as applied to model configuration, calibration, validation, salinity analysis, scenario evaluation, post-processing, and interpretation of results; and � Up to 50 hours of follow-on remote technical assistance and troubleshooting relating to the existing EEMS modeling workflow. The acquisition does not include purchase of a perpetual EEMS software license or three years of software maintenance. DSI has represented that it developed and solely owns EEMS and maintains the source code for EFDC+, EFDC+ Explorer, and Grid+. DSI further represents that knowledge of current-release features, workflows, and model options depends on its recent software development work; that it provides customized training and technical support directly to U.S. clients; and that it has no licensed or authorized U.S. distributors, resellers, or agents. Based on the Government�s current technical assessment and market research, USACE anticipates that DSI is the only source reasonably available to provide the required current-release, developer-level training and technical assistance. The Government will consider information submitted in response to this notice before making a final acquisition decision. Interested responsible sources may submit a written capability statement demonstrating their ability to meet the complete requirement. Responses should specifically address current-release EEMS expertise; the ability to provide project-specific, hands-on training and follow-on troubleshooting for EFDC+, EFDC+ Explorer, and Grid+; access to the technical knowledge needed to support the current release without reliance on DSI; relevant experience; and the proposed approach and timeframe for performance. General environmental modeling experience or familiarity with earlier software versions, without evidence of capability to meet the stated current-release requirements, may not establish the ability to perform this requirement. Submit capability statements electronically to Ligaya Lowe, Contract Specialist, at ligaya.m.lowe@usace.army.mil, with a copy to Gerald Garvey, Contracting Officer, at gerald.l.garvey@usace.army.mil, no later than the response deadline stated above. Include the firm�s legal name, UEI, point of contact, and a concise description of relevant capabilities. Telephone responses will not be accepted. All timely responses will be reviewed solely to determine whether a competitive acquisition approach is appropriate. A determination not to complete this proposed acquisition, based on responses to this notice, is within the Government�s discretion and will be documented in the acquisition file. description: This is a Sources Sought Notice Announcement only. This advertisement is not a solicitation for offers, nor is it a request for quotes. A request for quotes may be issued at a later date. Portland Area Indian Health Service is seeking responsible vendors to provide preventative maintenance service for the HVAC system, Chiller and Controls at the Fort Hall Service Unit (FHSU), Fort Hall, ID. The clinic requires preventative maintenance of the HVAC system to optimize facility operations and energy efficiency without interruptions to patient care. FHSU specializes in the promotion of comprehensive family healthy for federally recognized American Indian and Alaska Native people and their descendants. Contractors will be responsible for performing preventative maintenance services on the HVAC system, Chiller and Controls to ensure the facility is ventilated in accordance with the most current version of ASHRAE 170 � Ventilation of Health Care Facilities, and ASHRAE 62.1 � Ventilation for Acceptable Indoor Air Quality. title: HYDROSPHERE, BIOSPHERE, & GEOPHYSICS (HBG) SUPPORT SERVICES II - FINAL REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (FRFP)
description: UPDATE #1 � Amendment #0001 to the RFP was released on October 22, 2026. UPDATE #2 � Amendment #0002 to the RFP was released on October 26, 2026. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), hereby invites interested parties to review the Final Request for Proposal (FRFP) for the Hydrosphere, Biosphere, and Geophysics (HBG) Support Services II requirement supporting the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. The principal purpose of this requirement is to provide science research that conceives, develops, and applies space, field-deployed (i.e. airborne and in situ) and laboratory based technologies and observations to address issues of importance to society. These include but are not limited to water resources, land and ocean ecosystems, global and regional sea level change, changes in the Earth�s cryosphere, gravity field, magnetic field, solid Earth, and the terrestrial reference frame. The Statement of Work, Attachment A, describes the scope of the requirement. This contract is for support of a full range of science and research activities across the breadth of the various Laboratories that make up the HBG sub-division: the Cryospheric Sciences, Ocean Ecology, Hydrological Sciences, Biospheric Sciences, and Geodesy and Geophysics Laboratories. This contract is also for support of science, research and computing activities within the Terrestrial Information Systems Laboratory (TISL), also in the ESD. For the purposes of this document and contract the term HBG will be used to encompass all the Laboratories of the HBG sub-division and the TISL. NASA will conduct this acquisition as a small business set-aside. This competitive acquisition was originally contemplated as a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with the ability to issue CPFF task orders. Following further acquisition planning and assessment of the Government's requirements, the contract structure has been modified. The HBG II Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP) posted on April 8, 2025 was issued as an IDIQ CPFF solicitation. As amended, this competitive acquisition will now result in a HYBRID Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with the ability to issue Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) AND Firm- Fixed Price (FFP) task orders. The contract will have an effective ordering period of five years from the contract effective date. Interested offerors are encouraged to review the solicitation and all associated attachments for complete details regarding the requirements and proposal submission instructions. Please see the attached cover letter for additional information.

title: MH-60 Airborne Mine Countermeasure (AMCM) Carriage, Stream, Tow and Recovery System (CSTRS) Obsolescence Support
description: Introduction The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), in support of PMA-299 MH-60 Multi-Mission Helicopter Program Office, is seeking sources to support the Airborne Mine Countermeasure (AMCM) Carriage, Stream, Tow and Recovery System (CSTRS). The Contractor shall have the capability, experience, equipment, and facilities required to support ongoing obsolescence issues affecting CSTRS. Program Background AMCM was originally contracted in 2000 and executed in the DoD RDT&E funding under H2773, under which the first CSTRS prototypes were delivered to the U.S. Government. Carriage, Stream, Tow, and Recovery System (CSTRS) is part of the Airborne Mine Countermeasures (AMCM) weapons systems used on the MH-60S aircraft to allow the mounting, deployment, and recovery of Airborne Mine Neutralization System (AMNS) and Airborne Laser Mine Detection System (ALMDS). The Government requires mitigation strategies to address obsolescence issues within the AMCM CSTRS Mission Kit in support of the following: Provide sustainment support, system updates, and technical reach back for the existing AMCM CSTRS Mission Kits to combat rising obsolescence issues within the associated Weapons Replaceable Assemblies (WRAs) and Shop Replaceable Assemblies (SRAs). Proposed mitigation strategies and solutions shall be backwards compatible with all U.S. Navy MH-60S AMCM versions to include: � CSTRS Non-Tow Mission Kit part number 04101A01-03 � CSTRS Tow Mission Kit part number 09412 � CSTRS Base Mission Kit part number 09754A01-00 The Contractor shall design and implement solutions to address obsolete WRAs and SRAs, as appropriate, to facilitate improved logistical support for the AMCM CSTRS Mission Kit. The AMCM Mission Kit is comprised of the CSTRS Base Mission Kit, CSTRS Base Structure Assembly, Tow Mission Kit, and the Non-Tow Mission Kit. The Contractor shall provide form, fit, and function replacements as possible solutions to facilitate maintaining inventory without requiring replacement of currently fleeted WRAs/SRAs. The Contractor shall support aircraft testing, deliver a full Technical Data Package for all upgraded parts, deliver an Engineering Change Proposal (ECP) for incorporation into the current system configuration, and update all applicable logistical support data. The Contractor shall ensure solutions comply with AMCM System Specification 233A172, or a superseding specification revision approved by the Government, if made available prior to any contract award. Required Capabilities 1. Design solutions shall comply with the requirements of the MH-60S Airborne Mine Countermeasures (AMCM) System Specification, document number 233A172 Rev J, dated February 16, 2015, or its superseding Government-approved revision, whichever is available at potential contract award. This shall include all aspects of design, qualification, and testing of solutions. 2. Design solutions shall be backward compatible at the WRA/SRA level to AMCM CSTRS Mission Kit. 3. Design solutions shall provide the ability to support software growth capability for potential new software-driven modifications for the AMCM Winch Maintenance Laptop Software (WMLS). 4. Software updates, if needed, shall be backward compatible with current AMCM CSTRS Mission Kit configuration hardware and operating system. 5. Design solutions shall adhere to current U.S. Department of War cybersecurity requirements. 6. Provision of life cycle estimates for new components. 7. Provide documentation verifying solutions, when integrated into CSTRS, are safe for flight in support of U.S. Navy flight clearance processes. 8. Provide on-site and remote support to Government-conducted testing of final solutions. 9. Deliver to Government Level III Technical Data Packages for design solutions for this effort.
