title: Fuels Management Services at Malmstrom Air Force Base, MT and FE Warren Air Force Base, WY
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for fuels operations and management to include bulk storage services, retail service station support, alongside aircraft services, and entire fuels management services at two Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities, Malmstrom Air Force Base (AFB), MT and FE Warren AFB, WY. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense-Wide Working Capital Fund (DWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor shall provide sufficient general-purpose vehicles with appropriate capability to meet the contract requirements but not limited to escorting fuel deliveries where required, towing bowsers, transporting personnel, and performing expeditor duties as needed. The Contractor should provide sufficient special purpose vehicles with appropriate capability to meet the contract requirements for aviation and ground product services. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statements (PWS) tasks. Tasks identified in the PWS are performed by either the Contractor or Agency as specified in Appendix M The Contractor is responsible for staffing, operations, maintenance, safety, security, environmental protection, training, contractor-furnished items, and Contractor Detailed Plans related to the fuel operations at the location. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for fuel products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, inventory accuracy, and no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% restricted to Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) participation. Firms submitting a proposal under this RFP must be certified as SDVOSB by the Small Business Administration in accordance with FAR 19.1403. The NAICS Code is 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates awarding two firm fixed-price contracts. This requirement will be for a four-year base period (April 1, 2027 to March 31, 2031), a five-year option period (April 1, 2031 to March 31, 2036), and an option to extend the contract for up to six individual months (April 1, 2036 to September 30, 2036). This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources. Interested firms may submit proposals for one location or both locations. The solicitation will be published electronically on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) prior to submitting a proposal. The Date of the Pre-Preproposal conference, in conjunction with the sites visit will be listed in the solicitation. Offerors will be required to submit in writing to the Contract Specialist (via e-mail) the name(s) and email(s) of the individual(s) who plan to attend by 11:00 AM Eastern Time on October 22, 2026.

title: FIID Advanced Anti-Fraud and Risk-Modeling Proof of Concept
description: FEMA�s Fraud Investigations and Inspections Division (FIID), in coordination with the Office of the Chief Component Procurement Officer (OCCPO), is conducting market research to identify commercially available advanced anti-fraud and entity-risk modeling solutions for a potential competitive, multi-vendor Proof of Concept (POC). The POC would assess vendors� ability to identify potentially high-risk business entities using authorized data sources, fraud-risk indicators, and analytical methods, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, predictive analytics, rules engines, entity resolution, anomaly detection, graph and network analytics, identity and business verification, and optical character recognition. FEMA seeks scalable solutions that accurately identify potential risk while minimizing false positives and false negatives; provide transparent, reviewable explanations for alerts, risk scores, and entity assessments; integrate with cloud, hybrid, API-based, and batch-processing government environments; and support applicable federal security, privacy, accessibility, records-management, and data-governance requirements. The POC would be limited to evaluating technical capabilities and would not include live operational screening, grant eligibility determinations, adverse-action recommendations, or decisions affecting an individual�s or entity�s rights, benefits, eligibility, or safety. 1. Business Judgment Guidance for Prospective Offerors This notice is published to encourage open competition and to assist prospective offerors in determining if this requirement matches their technical capabilities. Who Should Respond: Vendors with demonstrated, scalable expertise in deploying enterprise-grade predictive analytics, anti-fraud algorithms, and network graph analysis in financial, commercial, or federal regulatory environments. Solicitation Request: A formal solicitation is not currently available. Responses to this RFI will directly shape the acquisition strategy and technical requirements for the competitive Proof of Concept phase.. 2. Attachments and Links Further program documentation, templates, and the RFI packet are attached to this notice on SAM.gov.

title: Request for Proposals (RFP) for Fresh Fruit & Vegetable support for DLA Troop Support's DoW Troop and Non-DoW School and Indian Tribal Organization customers located in Dallas, TX
description: The DLA Troop Support intends to solicit a full-line of produce support for DoD (Troop) customers and Non-DoD (USDA School & Indian Tribal Organization) customers located in the Dallas, Texas Zone. This acquisition will be issued on a small business set-aside (100%) basis. A waiver of the Non-Manufacturer rule has not been requested for this acquisition because it is an acquisition for multiple items. In accordance with 13 CFR 121.406(d)(1), if at least 50% of the estimated contract value of an acquisition for multiple items is composed of items that are manufactured by small business concerns, then a waiver of the Non-Manufacturer rule is not required. As such, for this acquisition, it is expected that items comprising at least 50% of the contract value will be manufactured by small business concerns. The contracting officer must be immediately notified if it appears as though this requirement will not be met. The total length of the contract will be five (5) years. It contains one (1) twenty-four (24) month tier, and two (2) eighteen (18) month tiers. Its estimated maximum total contract dollar value is $243,976,437.00. The delivery points require indefinite quantities of Fresh Fruit and Vegetables throughout the term of the contract. A more detailed listing of the delivery sites can be found in the solicitation. All responsible sources may submit proposals that will be considered by DLA Troop Support. The Government will award a contract(s) resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror(s) whose offer(s) conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The source selection method for this procurement will be the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) source selection procedures and shall use the following to evaluate offers: 1. Technical Acceptability - A technically acceptable offer is an offer that takes no exceptions to the terms and conditions in the solicitation and complies fully with all submission requirements, including submissions relating to the two subfactors listed below. A proposal that takes exception to solicitation terms and conditions or that fails to comply with all submission requirements may be deemed technically unacceptable and, thus, may be found ineligible, and removed from further consideration for the award. By submitting a proposal with no exceptions, an offeror is confirming it possesses the necessary facilities, equipment, technical skills and capacity to successfully provide all items required by this solicitation. The following sub-factors will be evaluated and must be found acceptable for a proposal to be eligible for award: A. Perishable Agricultural Commodities Act (PACA) License - The offeror shall possess and submit proof of a valid current PACA license. B. USDA Harmonized Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) Plus + Standard Audit with warehouse and food defense addenda and/or USDA Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) audit - The Contracting Officer will require an offeror to submit a valid USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard audit, including addenda for warehouse and food defense, and/or USDA GMP audit, or an independent third-party certifying company audit report(s) / certificate for each place of performance identified in the offeror's proposal. The audit report(s) must demonstrate a passing score in the following parts: General, Warehouse and Food Defense addenda. In lieu of a USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard and/or USDA GMP audit report / certificate, the offeror may submit an audit report / certificate conducted by a recognized private independent third-party certifying company certifying to an industry recognized food safety standard that exceeds all aspects of the USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard audit and/or USDA GMP report / certificate requirements. Offerors relying on a non-USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard and/or USDA GMP audit report / certificate that do not agree to have a USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard and/or USDA GMP audit report / certificate for each place of performance prior to the start of contract performance will be found technically unacceptable. 2. Pricing - Pricing is required for all items found in the Schedule of Items (for Group 1 and 2 (2a and 2b), if applicable) and for all tiers. Failure to offer pricing for all items and for all tiers may result in a proposal being removed from consideration for award as technically unacceptable. The Government will perform an aggregate price analysis on all items found in the Schedule of Items (for Group 1 and 2 (2a and 2b), if applicable). To determine an offeror's Evaluated Aggregate Price for Group 1, the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price will be added to the Aggregate Delivered Price. To determine an offeror's Evaluated Aggregate Price Group 2 (2a and 2b), the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price will be added to the Aggregate Delivered Price for each sub-group 2a and 2b, respectively, to come to a preliminary Evaluated Aggregate Price for each sub-group. Then, the preliminary Evaluated Aggregate price for 2a and 2b will be added together to determine the offeror's Evaluated Aggregate Price for Group 2. Please refer to paragraph (d) below for further details regarding these price components. The award(s) will be made on the basis of the lowest Evaluated Aggregate Price (for each group) of proposals meeting or exceeding the acceptability standards for non-price factors. The Government reserves the right to remove item(s) from the Schedule of Items. Prior to award, the offered prices of the presumptive awardee(s) will be evaluated on an individual line-item basis to determine whether each price is fair and reasonable using analytical techniques deemed appropriate by the Contracting Officer in her/his complete discretion. A. Price Components: 1. Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price: Aggregate Distribution Price is obtained by first multiplying the proposed distribution price for each item in the Schedule of Items by the item's estimated quantity to calculate the total distribution price for each item. Then, the total distribution prices of all items will be added together to determine the total distribution price for tier 1. The total distribution price for each subsequent tier will also be calculated. The total distribution prices for all tiers will be added together to determine the Aggregate Distribution Price. The Aggregate Distribution Price is then multiplied by a weighting factor of 6 to arrive at the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price. Note: the weighting factor is applied only to the overall Aggregate Distribution Price (not on a line item basis), and is to be used for evaluation purposes only. The Government's use of a weighting factor of 6 for distribution pricing is done in order to more accurately balance the significance of the pricing components and their respective impact on any subsequent contract(s) issued under this solicitation. 2. Aggregate Delivered Price: The Aggregate Delivered Price is obtained by first multiplying the proposed delivered price of each item in the Schedule of Items by the item's estimated quantity to calculate the total delivered price for each item. Then, the total delivered prices of all items will be added together to determine the total delivered price for tier 1. The total delivered price for each subsequent tier will also be calculated. The total delivered prices for all tiers will be added together to determine the Aggregate Delivered Price. 3. Evaluated Aggregate Price: The Evaluated Aggregate Price is obtained by adding the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price and Aggregate Delivered Price together. 4. For purposes of the Price Proposal Evaluation, Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price and Aggregate Delivered Price are considered equal. This equality is accounted for mathematically by applying a weighting factor of 6 (based on current Government data) to the Aggregate Distribution Price. Option

description: Page 7 of 7 REQUEST FOR INFORMATION THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veterans Health Administration (VHA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) as market research to determine the availability of vendors that can provide a Veteran Transportation Software Solution (Vetride) with VHA enterprise-wide licensing that includes all requirements identified in the attached Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS). The VA is not, at this time, seeking proposals or quotes, and therefore, will not accept, review, or evaluate unsolicited proposals or quotes received in response hereto. This notice is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted because of this request. It supports decentralized operations in which each VA medical center manages transportation for Veterans in its service area and offers reimbursement for medically related travel. title: Office of Space Commerce BPA
description: Description THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY � Solicitations are not available at this time. Requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the United States Government and respondents will not be entitled to payment of direct or indirect cost incurred in responding to this request for information (RFI). The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Acquisition and Grants Office (AGO), Corporate Services Acquisition Division (CSAD), located in Silver Spring, MD, is conducting market research to identify businesses and organizations capable of providing specialized space policy research, analysis, consultation, data services, and strategic advisory support. The Government is also seeking information on industry capabilities and approaches for providing flexible, on-demand access to qualified subject matter experts, including short-notice consultations, rapid-turn analyses, and longer-duration support. Responses will help assess the availability of qualified sources, industry capacity to meet varying response timelines, and potential acquisition approaches, including consideration of a multiple-award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA). NAICS CODE: To be determined Background The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Office of Space Commerce (OSC), is the principal unit for space commerce policy activities within the Department of Commerce. OSC's mission is to foster the conditions for the economic growth and technological advancement of the U.S. commercial space industry. Within OSC, the Policy, Advocacy, and International Division (PAID) supports the development and coordination of domestic and international space commerce policies, promotes U.S. commercial space interests, and engages with government, industry, and international stakeholders on emerging space policy issues. Given the rapidly evolving commercial space environment, PAID requires timely access to specialized expertise, research, data, and analysis to support policy development, strategic planning, and leadership decision-making. These needs may arise with little advance notice and range from brief consultations with subject matter experts to comprehensive research, policy assessments, and longer-duration advisory support. PAID is exploring approaches to obtaining these services that provide flexibility, timely access to qualified experts, and cost-effective support across a broad range of space policy matters. Purpose The purpose of this RFI is to better understand industry capabilities, service delivery approaches, and associated costs and benefits for providing flexible, on-demand space policy research, analysis, consultation, data services, and strategic advisory support. Specifically, the Government seeks information on vendors' demonstrated expertise across the identified Task Areas, their ability to provide timely access to qualified subject matter experts, and their capacity to support both short-duration consultations and more extensive analytical requirements. The Government is also interested in understanding whether these capabilities are available through vendors' existing personnel, established subcontractor or consultant relationships, or other arrangements. Responses will assist OSC in refining its requirements, evaluating potential acquisition and ordering approaches, and determining how best to obtain timely, cost-effective access to specialized expertise. Although this RFI requests specific information, it is not intended to discourage creative thinking on the part of the industry to propose alternative solutions or approaches that the Government may not have considered. Scope and Draft Requirements The attached draft PWS describes seven potential task areas. Respondents may identify one or more areas of demonstrated capability: Commercial Space Policy and Regulation � U.S. commercial space policy, licensing, permitting, regulatory oversight, and interagency issues. Space Traffic Coordination, Safety, and Sustainability � Civil space traffic coordination, SSA, conjunction coordination, debris mitigation, standards and norms. International and Geopolitical Space Policy � International governance, UNCOPUOS, foreign regulatory regimes, geopolitical implications. Space Law and Regulatory Analysis � Domestic/international legal and regulatory research and analysis; not legal representation. Commercial Space Industry and Economic Policy � Commercial space markets, competitiveness, investment, industry data, indicators and economic impacts. Emerging Space Activities and Technology Policy � Policy implications of RPO, in-space servicing, commercial stations, lunar activities, remote sensing and novel services. Strategic and Executive Advisory Support � Expert consultations, executive briefings, workshops, time-sensitive research and decision-support analysis. Potential forms of support include: Consultation Only; Consultation Plus Summary; Research and Analytical Services; Data and Information Services; and Extended Support. Services may be ordered individually or together. The draft PWS describes Rapid (several hours to one business day), Expedited (generally one to two business days), and Standard quotation/availability response categories. These are response expectations, not automatic performance-completion deadlines. The contemplated BPA would have a five-year ordering period, with requirements, schedules, deliverables and pricing established at the individual Call level. The Government has not determined the final acquisition vehicle, number of awards, or ordering procedures. Responses Responses to this RFI must be submitted using the Market Research Questionnaire located at https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdnCIev0vZbNRslzShVW9nCFj-Pe_UgXVdsSmlADasb05Fztg/viewform by Friday, December 8, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

title: Depot Intermediate Level and Non-Recurring (DINRE) FY30-34
description: The F-35 Lightning II Joint Program Office (JPO) intends to award a sole-source contract to Lockheed Martin Corporation, Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Company (LM Aero), Fort Worth, Texas, for F-35 non-recurring sustainment support. The scope being procured under the Depot, Intermediate Level, and Non-Recurring Engineering (DINRE) contract includes: Depot Activation; Intermediate-level Maintenance; Sustainment Non-Recurring Engineering Efforts; Reliability, Maintainability, and Health Maturation; Structural Integrity Program and Low Observable Maturation; Structural Integrity Program and Low Observable Maturation; Depot Analysis, Planning, and Implementation; Depot Material Lay-In (MLI); Depot Material Activation; Depot Test Systems Development and Support; eCASS (electronic consolidated automated support system) Repair, Test, and Check; Depot-specific Support Equipment (SE); Maintenance Plan Change (MPC) project opportunities; and organic software maintenance support capabilities. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole-source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1)), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." LM Aero is the original designer, developer, and manufacturer of the F-35 aircraft and is the only source with the capabilities required to provide sustainment support for F-35 aircraft. LM Aero solely possesses the proprietary design knowledge, technical data rights, and engineering capabilities required to perform this highly specialized work. Because the DINRE contract represents an integrated, highly complex requirement of non-recurring activations and engineering efforts, breaking out individual activation tasks, regional depot lines, or test program sets to alternate vendors is economically and operationally impracticable. Attempting to segregate these tasks would require the Government to duplicate massive, cost-prohibitive systems-engineering overhead and fund redundant tooling. Furthermore, separating technical responsibility across multiple contractors would introduce severe integration risks, void OEM performance warranties, and delay critical organic depot stand-ups, directly degrading fleet-wide mission-capable rates. The DINRE FY30�34 contract is anticipated to be awarded during FY30, supporting the U.S. Services, Cooperative Program Partners, and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) Customers. This notice of intent is neither a request for proposal nor a solicitation of offers. However, in accordance with FAR 5.207(c)(16)(ii), all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation that will be considered by the U.S. Government. Based upon any responses to this notice, the U.S. Government reserves the right to process this procurement action on a sole-source basis. For availability of subcontracting opportunities, contact LM Aero.

title: Maintenance and Repair of Anesthesia Units at Brian D. Allgood Army Community Hospital and All Outlying Clinics, USAMEDDAC-Korea
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The Government intends to award one purchase order. Solicitation number HT941027QE001 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for a firm fixed-price, non-personal service contract for Maintenance and Repair of Anesthesia Units at Brian D. Allgood Army Community Hospital and All Outlying Clinics, USAMEDDAC-Korea. This requirement is for a period of performance from 01 January 2027 through 31 December 2027 (Base Period), plus four (4), one-year option periods and FAR 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services. description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT DEPARTMENT OF THE NAVY Program Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) Capability Portfolio Executive Combat Systems & Fires (CPE CS&F) Integrated Combat System (ICS), PMW 630 SECTION 1: GENERAL INFORMATION Document Type: Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Notice Solicitation / Reference Number: N6175027R1201 Contracting Activity: Navy PAE Mission Systems, Washington Navy Yard, DC Program Title: Surface Ship ICS Engineering and Integration North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 541330 � Engineering Services (Military and Aerospace Equipment and Military Weapons) Product Service Code (PSC): AC13 � R&D: Defense Systems: Weapons / R425 � Support - Professional: Engineering/Technical Response Due Date: 04 December 2026, 15:00 EST Classification Level: Primary document UNCLASSIFIED. Classified responses or annexes up to SECRET / NOFORN handled by separate coordination (see Section 7). SECTION 2: STATUTORY DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICE This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with FAR 15.101(c). This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an announcement of a forthcoming solicitation. Issuance of this notice does not obligate the Government to issue a formal solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not pay or reimburse any costs incurred by respondents in preparing, submitting, or demonstrating information in response to this notice. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Participation in this RFI is voluntary. Failure to respond will not preclude a vendor from participating in any future competitive acquisition, should one be released. Respondents may submit capability statements addressing any subset or all of the focus areas detailed herein. SECTION 3: BACKGROUND & PROGRAM CONTEXT 3.1 Background & Context Modern surface warfare requires rapid, modular capability delivery across the Navy's surface fleet. The Navy�s ICS program is making this vision a reality through use of virtualization, Kubernetes orchestration, and development of a common suite of mission applications enabling a "build once and deploy across the fleet" methodology for delivery of capability to frigates, destroyers, amphibious ships, aircraft carriers, future manned and unmanned vessels, and future foreign military sales vessels. The ICS program is conducting market research to identify industry partners capable of executing comprehensive systems engineering and software integration for U.S. Navy surface combat systems. This scope is currently being executed under the N00024-23-C-5117 contract awarded to Lockheed Martin Rotary & Mission Systems in September 2023. 3.2 Technical Scope & Baselines The technical scope spans current and next-generation baseline configurations running incremental deliveries of the Integrated Combat System (ICS) software stack (infrastructure services and tactical platform services) and common mission applications. Applicable ship deliveries include the following: ICS-Enabled AEGIS Combat System Baselines 9.C3+ and Baseline 10.1+ running on Mk6 Mod0/1 hardware with IaaS ORDALT or on Mk6 ModX hardware ICS-Enabled Ship Self-Defense System (SSDS) platforms FF(X) 3 and follow DDG 1000 class in line with delivery of the Zumwalt Enterprise Upgrade Solution (ZEUS) Future USN and FMS platforms SECTION 4: TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS & CAPABILITY AREAS SOUGHT The Navy seeks detailed technical capabilities, corporate competencies, and innovative methodologies across eleven (11) functional areas. Vendors may respond to any or all of the following scope areas: Focus Area 1: Programmatic Engineering, Configuration Management & Governance Configuration Management (CM): Formulating, baselining, and executing Configuration Management Plans (CMP), software build/release planning, Configuration Control Boards (CCBs), and tracking and adjudicating Software Change Requests (SWCRs). Programmatic & Systems Planning: Developing, maintaining, and synchronizing project-level Roadmaps, Integrated Master Schedules (IMS), and capability delivery cadences. Focus Area 2: Systems Engineering & Requirements Architecture Technical Baseline Artifacts: Developing, updating, and managing formal engineering artifacts: Systems Engineering Plans (SEP). Software Development Plans (SDP) utilizing modern Agile/DevSecOps frameworks. System / Subsystem Definition Documents (SSDD). System / Subsystem Specifications (SSS). Software Product Specifications (SPS). Interface Requirements Specifications (IRS). Requirements Traceability Verification Matrices (RTVM) maintaining end-to-end bidirectional requirement-to-test traceability. System Safety Plans (SSP) conforming to MIL-STD-882E and naval weapon safety requirements. Requirements Allocation: Decomposing ICS, AEGIS, SSDS, and future combat system Top Level Requirements (TLR) into modular capability building blocks and subsystem specifications across surface ship classes (DDG 51, CG 47, FF(X), DDG 1000, L-Class, CVN, unmanned surface vessels, FMS variants, future platforms). Technical Leadership: Serving as lead technical authorities in Integrated Product Teams (IPTs), Working Groups (WGs), formal milestone reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR), and leading Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMs) to define and allocate interface requirements. Force-Level Mission Thread Analysis: Evaluating complex, distributed kill-chain mission threads, establishing functional allocations, and resolving tactical latency challenges. ICS Re-Architecture & Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE): Authoring SysML/UML MBSE models and leading modular product development across the ICS Domain Architecture. Sensor Management. Vehicle Management. Information Management. Training Management. Tactical Decision Management. External Communications Management. Weapon Management. Display Management. Infrastructure Services. Focus Area 3: Fleet Data Analysis, Feasibility Studies & Gap Assessment Conducting engineering feasibility studies, system performance assessments, and trade studies for capability insertion across diverse ship classes and configurations. Extracting, parsing, and analyzing live fleet exercise data, weapon telemetry, and real-world tactical events to identify performance anomalies and drive capability enhancement. Assessing combat system shortfalls, bottlenecks, and operational gaps, and designing/evaluating candidate architectural and software modifications to close these gaps. Focus Area 4: Tactical Software Design, Coding, Testing, and Integration Combat System Design activities including analysis and algorithm development Mission software development, unit testing, and component integration. Cloud-based and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL)-based testing to include element integration, subsystem testing, and system testing System Integration: Engineering and integrating software interfaces for specific sensor, weapon, and C2 programs and capabilities, including but not limited to: Patriot Advanced Capability-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (PAC-3 MSE) The Standard Missile (SM) Family of weapons (including all Air Defense, Ballistic Missile Defense, and Extended Range Active Missile variants) MK-41 VLS-compatible canister-launched weapons (including Evolved SeaSparrow Missile (ESSM), Tomahawk Land Attack Missile (TLAM), and Vertical Launch ASROC (VLA) Rolling Airframe Missile (RAM) Electronic Warfare (EW) systems Phased array and rotating radar systems Evolving to common track management solution across AEGIS and SSDS configurations Containerized payloads Tactical Virtualization Configurations: Designing, provisioning, benchmarking, and troubleshooting virtualized tactical hardware/software configurations and hypervisor-to-bare-metal runtime environments. Focus Area 5: Hardware/Software Tech Stack, Microservices & System-of-Systems Integration Third-Party Software & Micro

title: Depot Intermediate Level and Non-Recurring Engineering (DINRE) FY30-34
description: The F-35 Lightning II Joint Program Office (JPO) intends to award a sole-source contract to Lockheed Martin Corporation, Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Company (LM Aero), Fort Worth, Texas, for F-35 non-recurring sustainment support. The scope being procured under the Depot, Intermediate Level, and Non-Recurring Engineering (DINRE) contract includes: Depot Activation; Intermediate-level Maintenance; Sustainment Non-Recurring Engineering Efforts; Reliability, Maintainability, and Health Maturation; Structural Integrity Program and Low Observable Maturation; Structural Integrity Program and Low Observable Maturation; Depot Analysis, Planning, and Implementation; Depot Material Lay-In (MLI); Depot Material Activation; Depot Test Systems Development and Support; eCASS (electronic consolidated automated support system) Repair, Test, and Check; Depot-specific Support Equipment (SE); Maintenance Plan Change (MPC) project opportunities; and organic software maintenance support capabilities. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole-source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1)), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." LM Aero is the original designer, developer, and manufacturer of the F-35 aircraft and is the only source with the capabilities required to provide sustainment support for F-35 aircraft. LM Aero solely possesses the proprietary design knowledge, technical data rights, and engineering capabilities required to perform this highly specialized work. Because the DINRE contract represents an integrated, highly complex requirement of non-recurring activations and engineering efforts, breaking out individual activation tasks, regional depot lines, or test program sets to alternate vendors is economically and operationally impracticable. Attempting to segregate these tasks would require the Government to duplicate massive, cost-prohibitive systems-engineering overhead and fund redundant tooling. Furthermore, separating technical responsibility across multiple contractors would introduce severe integration risks, void OEM performance warranties, and delay critical organic depot stand-ups, directly degrading fleet-wide mission-capable rates. The DINRE FY30�34 contract is anticipated to be awarded during FY30, supporting the U.S. Services, Cooperative Program Partners, and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) Customers. This notice of intent is neither a request for proposal nor a solicitation of offers. However, in accordance with FAR 5.207(c)(16)(ii), all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation that will be considered by the U.S. Government. Based upon any responses to this notice, the U.S. Government reserves the right to process this procurement action on a sole-source basis. For availability of subcontracting opportunities, contact LM Aero.

title: Refurbishment of Existing Tree Cooler, St. Joe Ranger District, Idaho Panhandle National Forests
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 1284LL27Q0008 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) Refurbishment of Existing Tree Cooler. Services and supplies are required for the currently installed tree cooler for the St. Joe Ranger District, Idaho Panhandle National Forests. The tree cooler was built in 1984, the outdated HVAC system shall be replaced with a new HVAC system. The contractor shall provide a fully functioning new HVAC system for the existing tree cooler with associated evaporator fans and necessary materials for the refrigeration system. Contractor shall remove any humidifiers and associated parts, update the lighting, and install a notification system of a power outage due to ongoing power fluctuations. The contractor shall provide the personnel, materials, and equipment needed to perform the required services to industry standards and specifications. Representative shall communicate with POC regarding any issues that may arise. Contractor shall coordinate work hours with CO and COR for site access, hours, and operation. There will be no Government Property issued. Electricity will be available on site for Contractor's use. All work shall be completed by 03/15/2027. See attachment 1284LL27Q0008 for more details. Amendment issued on 11/20/2026, see attachment 1284LL27Q0008_0001 for more information. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 811310 The small business size standard is $12.5 million dollars. This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency.

REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. QA personnel shall maintain a complete receipt inspection,test, repair re-test, history card for each item processed. This information shall be made available to the Government upon request. 4. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 3.5 Additive Manufacturing- If/When Additive Manufacturing election taken by vendor, to maintain visibilityover Additively Manufactured components within the supply chain, Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) DD1423 reporting mechanisms apply. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4.
